In Re: An application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal
 Procedure filed on 08.09.2023 in connection with Santipur Police
 Station Case No.219 of 2018 dated 23.06.2018 under Sections
 498A/307/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
(G.R. Case No.1025 of 2018)

And
 In Re: Laxman Mistry
 ... ... Petitioner
 Mr. Ashok Das
 Mr. Sourav Mukherjee
 ... ... for the petitioner
 Mr. Debabrata Chatterjee .. ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor
 Mr. Santanu Chatterjee
 ... ... for the State
 1.
It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that he is in custody for about 53 days.
It is further submitted petitioner has been falsely implicated.
Investigation is complete.
Accordingly, he prays for bail.
2. Learned Advocate for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
3. We have considered the materials on record including the medical papers.
Admission report gives an impression victim had taken sleeping pills.
Allegations of torture are general and omnibus.
Investigation is complete.
There is no chance of absoncdence of the petitioner.
Under such circumstances and in view of the period of detention suffered by the petitioner, we are of the opinion further detention of the accused/petitioner is not necessary.

4. Therefore, the accused/petitioner, namely Laxman Mistry, be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten thousand only), with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Ranaghat, Nadia subject to condition that the said petitioner shall appear before the trial court on every date of hearing until further orders and shall not intimidate witnesses or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.
498A/307/34 Of The Indian Penal Code.
